# Jonas Lindqvist — Senior Cloud & Data Engineer — Hamburg, Germany (jonas.lindqvist@example.com)

# November 14, 2026
Six months into our warehouse migration project at Alsterkran Logistics Tech GmbH, and we finally turned off the last legacy SQL Server reporting instance yesterday afternoon at 16:40. No fanfare, just a quiet chat message from @Mareike Vossen confirming the final finance dashboard had cut over to Snowflake and dbt Core without a single ticket from accounting.

When I joined in May 2025, our nightly batch window was creeping past 07:30 every Tuesday, which meant dispatch leads in Hamburg were staring at stale container figures during morning standups. Over the last eighteen months, our four-person data platform squad rebuilt the ingestion layer on AWS (S3, Glue, ECS Fargate, and Terraform) and moved transformation logic into modular dbt models tested via GitHub Actions.

A few concrete numbers from the retrospective we ran this morning:
- End-to-end warehouse refresh dropped from 6 hours 40 minutes to 38 minutes.
- Monthly AWS compute and storage spend went down by roughly 29 percent.
- On-call alerts between midnight and 06:00 dropped to zero since August.

Huge thanks to @Tarek Al-Mansoor and @Mareike Vossen for reviewing dozens of pull requests while we untangled fifteen-year-old stored procedures. #DataEngineering #Snowflake #dbt #AWS #Terraform #HamburgTech

# August 28, 2026
Passed the AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional exam (SAP-C02) this morning with a score of 842 out of 1000.

I kept postponing the renewal because hands-on architecture work at Alsterkran Logistics Tech kept me busy enough, but preparing for the exam actually forced me to revisit multi-account AWS Organizations patterns, Transit Gateway routing quirks, and cost allocation tags that we ended up applying directly to our staging environment last month. #AWS #CloudArchitecture #ContinuousLearning

# March 19, 2026
Unpopular opinion in data engineering circles: most mid-sized freight companies do not need real-time Kafka streaming for every single operational table.

Last week a stakeholder asked if we could stream container yard updates with sub-second latency. Instead of spinning up a managed MSK cluster right away, @Svenja Kröger and I sat down with the dispatchers to watch how they actually work. Turns out they refresh their yard board every fifteen minutes before assigning trucks. We built an incremental micro-batch pipeline in Python and Apache Airflow running every five minutes on ECS, taking four days to ship instead of six weeks. #DataEngineering #ApacheAirflow #Python # November 03, 2025
Six months at Alsterkran Logistics Tech GmbH! Moving from Berlin to Hamburg in spring was a big personal step, and I will admit I had doubts about switching from a pure data consultancy to an in-house role in maritime software.

What surprised me most is how satisfying it is to live with the systems you build. In consulting, you hand over the repository, present the final slide deck, and move on to the next client before the first real schema drift hits production. Here, if I write a brittle ingestion script on Monday, I am the one fixing it on Thursday. That feedback loop makes you a much more disciplined engineer. Grateful to my team lead @Henrikje Paulsen for the trust since day one. #CareerUpdate #InHouseEngineering #Hamburg

# May 02, 2025
First week as Senior Cloud & Data Engineer at Alsterkran Logistics Tech GmbH here in Hamburg!

My desk near the harbor is set up, Docker and pyenv are finally cooperating on the new corporate laptop, and I merged my first tiny pull request today (fixing a hardcoded S3 bucket name in a Terraform module — we have all been there). Looking forward to helping the team modernize our freight analytics platform over the coming year. If you are around Hamburg and want to grab a coffee to talk Python, data modeling, or running routes, drop me a message! #NewJob #DataEngineering #CloudEngineering

# April 18, 2025
Today is my last day at Havelstrom Data Consulting GmbH in Berlin after wonderful three and a half years.

I walked into the office in October 2021 as a mid-level Data Engineer who knew how to write decent PySpark jobs and SQL queries, but still got nervous whenever a client asked about VPC peering, IAM permission boundaries, or why their Apache Spark executors were running out of off-heap memory. Walking out today as a Senior Data Engineer, having led technical delivery across four major client accounts in retail, renewable energy, and manufacturing.

A few highlights I will carry with me:
- Designing a greenfield lakehouse on Azure Databricks and Delta Lake for our wind park client Boreas Windkraftwerke AG, processing 1.4 TB of sensor telemetry per day.
- Mentoring three junior engineers through our internal engineering onboarding (@Lukas Brenner, you are going to do great leading the retail account!).
- Surviving the infamous December 2023 schema migration weekend fueled by black tea and cold pizza.

Thank you to @Dr. Miriam Kästner and the entire Havelstrom crew. After a short break to pack boxes and hand over my Berlin apartment keys, a new chapter in Hamburg starts in May! #Farewell #BerlinTech #ConsultingLife #DataEngineering # January 22, 2025
Wrapped up our internal knowledge-sharing session at Havelstrom Data Consulting on migrating legacy Apache Airflow 1.10 DAGs to Airflow 2.9 using the TaskFlow API and KubernetesExecutor.

Over the past four months, our project team helped a mid-market industrial client, Märkische Gießereiwerke GmbH, retire 140 tangled cron jobs and bash scripts scattered across three virtual machines. By standardizing on containerized Python tasks, strict Pydantic schema validation at the ingestion boundary, and Great Expectations checks before loading into PostgreSQL and BigQuery, we cut data quality incidents reported by controlling by over 60 percent in Q4 2024.

I put a public summary of our Pydantic validation pattern on my technical blog at https://jonas-lindqvist-notes.example.org/airflow-pydantic-patterns. Happy to discuss how others handle schema evolution in messy ERP exports! #ApacheAirflow #Python #DataQuality #Kubernetes #SQL

# September 14, 2024
Honored to be promoted to Senior Data Engineer at Havelstrom Data Consulting GmbH this month!

When @Dr. Miriam Kästner and I looked back at my goals from 2022, the biggest shift was not learning another framework — it was learning how to translate ambiguous business questions into reliable technical scope, push back politely when deadlines do not match data reality, and leave client teams more self-sufficient than we found them. Thank you to everyone who gave me honest code reviews and architecture feedback along the way. #Promotion #DataEngineering #CareerGrowth

# April 09, 2024
Just came back from speaking at the Berlin Data & Python Evening hosted at the offices of Spreebogen Cloud Systems GmbH!

My 25-minute talk was titled "Why Your Spark Job Is Waiting on One Partition: Practical Skew Mitigation in PySpark 3.4". We walked through an anonymized case from a wind telemetry project where a single faulty weather station ID accounted for 38 percent of all incoming rows, causing a four-hour bottleneck in a join stage. Showed how combining Adaptive Query Execution (AQE) settings with deterministic salting keys brought the stage runtime down to 11 minutes. Slides are online at https://slides.example.com/lindqvist-pyspark-skew-2024. #PySpark #ApacheSpark #Polars #Python

# November 17, 2023
Completed the Databricks Certified Data Engineer Professional certification today.

Since our client work over the past fourteen months at Havelstrom Data Consulting has been heavily focused on Azure Databricks, Unity Catalog, Delta Live Tables, and Terraform provider integrations, the exam felt very close to our daily engineering challenges. Biggest practical takeaway: investing two weeks upfront into clean Unity Catalog metastore governance and service principal permissions saves months of painful refactoring later. #Databricks #DeltaLake #Azure #DataGovernance # June 05, 2023
Reflections after nine months on a tough manufacturing analytics project: technical debt in data pipelines rarely comes from lazy engineers. Almost always, it comes from temporary hotfixes applied to upstream ERP systems that nobody told the data team about.

Last Tuesday, an order status column in an upstream extract silently switched from integer codes (10, 20, 30) to two-letter strings ("OP", "PR", "CL") for a single subsidiary. Because we had added Great Expectations assertions and automated alerting on the bronze-to-silver boundary back in February, our pipeline halted cleanly before corrupting the executive revenue tables in Snowflake. Took us forty minutes to patch the mapping table and backfill. Defensive data engineering is not glamorous, but it lets everyone sleep through the night. #DataQuality #DataEngineering #SQL

# October 11, 2022
One year at Havelstrom Data Consulting GmbH!

Over the past twelve months in Berlin, I have worked on two completely different stacks:
- Months 1 to 5: Helping a digital publishing client, Kupferdruck Medienhaus GmbH, migrate their self-hosted PostgreSQL analytics database and custom Python ETL scripts to Google Cloud Platform (BigQuery, Cloud Composer, Cloud Run, and Terraform).
- Months 6 to 12: Building PySpark streaming and batch pipelines on Azure for Boreas Windkraftwerke AG.

Switching cloud providers every six months was intimidating at first, but once you understand the underlying fundamentals — distributed storage, columnar file formats like Parquet, idempotent orchestration, IAM least privilege, and CI/CD via GitLab CI — the vendor-specific names are just vocabulary. #CloudComputing #GCP #Azure #DataEngineering #Python

# October 04, 2021
Excited to share that I have started a new position as Data Engineer at Havelstrom Data Consulting GmbH in Berlin!

After finishing my Master's degree and spending nearly two years building backend and data services in Kiel, I wanted to dive deeper into large-scale distributed data platforms and cloud infrastructure. Looking forward to working with a super sharp team of engineers and analysts right here in Berlin. #NewBeginnings #Berlin #DataEngineer #Python #Cloud

# September 17, 2021
Officially graduated! Today I received my final certificate for the M.Sc. in Data Science & Software Engineering from Holsten-Technikum — Private Hochschule für Informatik in Kiel (final grade: 1.3).

My master's thesis, supervised by Prof. Dr. Arndt Lohmeyer, focused on "Automated Anomaly Detection in Maritime Vessel Fuel Consumption Time Series Using Gradient Boosted Trees and Streaming Window Aggregations". I built the prototype in Python (scikit-learn, LightGBM, Pandas, FastAPI) and evaluated it on two years of historical vessel telemetry logs. Next stop: moving to Berlin at the end of the month! #Graduation #MScDataScience #MachineLearning #Kiel # March 29, 2021
Small open-source milestone: my pull request to a community Python library for parsing NMEA 0183 maritime sensor sentences was merged over the weekend!

At Schwentine Reederei-Software GmbH in Kiel, where I work part-time as a Junior Backend & Data Developer alongside my master's studies, we kept hitting edge cases with malformed checksums from older onboard GPS receivers. Fixed the parser bug, added pytest property-based tests using Hypothesis, and reduced parsing overhead by about 18 percent on 5 million sample records. Glad we could upstream the fix instead of maintaining a private fork. #OpenSource #Python #Pytest #SoftwareEngineering

# November 12, 2019
Started a new role as Working Student — Backend & Data Engineering at Schwentine Reederei-Software GmbH in Kiel!

I will be supporting the engineering team 20 hours a week while pursuing my M.Sc. in Data Science & Software Engineering at Holsten-Technikum in Kiel. In my first two weeks, I have already been writing Python microservices with Flask, optimizing slow TimescaleDB / PostgreSQL queries for vessel tracking dashboards, and learning how Docker Compose and GitLab CI pipelines work in a real production environment. Nothing beats seeing your own SQL query optimization cut a customer dashboard load time from 14 seconds to under 800 milliseconds. #WorkingStudent #PostgreSQL #Python #Docker

# September 24, 2019
Finished my B.Sc. in Computer Science (Informatik) at Trave-Akademie für Technik und Wirtschaft in Lübeck last week and already packed my bags to move one hour north to Kiel for my Master's program!

Big thank you to everyone at Marzipanstadt Handelssysteme GmbH in Lübeck, where I spent my mandatory six-month internship and wrote my bachelor's thesis on automated ETL error recovery with Python and PostgreSQL (grade: 1.7). That internship convinced me that sitting at the intersection of backend software engineering and data infrastructure is exactly what I want to do long-term. Onward to the next adventure! #ComputerScience #BSc #DataEngineering #FirstSteps
